title: Govt defers Census 2027 in Manipur amid protests, demand for NRC
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Union government on Monday deferred the 2027 census in Manipur amid mounting violence and demands by large chunks of the population to update the National Register of Citizens (NRC) before conducting the population enumeration exercise.

Adding to this, Imphal: Women take part in protest rally 'Meira Rally' as they hold flame torches demanding updation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC) before the Census in Manipur, at Khurai area, in Imphal on Aug. 21 (PTI FILE) The development came a day before the house-listing of the census exercise was scheduled to begin in the strife-torn state, where nearly 300 have died since May 2023.

Meanwhile, The decision came after Union home minister Amit Shah chaired a high-level review meeting in New Delhi to “assess the current situation” in Manipur, according to a statement from the chief minister’s office.

Notably, “The meeting held at the ministry of home affairs was attended by the governor of Manipur, Shri Ajay Kumar Bhalla, chief minister Shri Yumnam Khemchand Singh, home secretary Shri Govind Mohan, along with other senior officials. The meeting discussed in detail the demand raised by the people of Manipur to defer the Census exercise in the State before the implementation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC). The meeting agreed to defer the proposed census exercise in the state considering the feelings and aspirations of the people of Manipur,” the statement shared.

As per the latest buzz, The census exercise has been disrupted by violence in the past, such as in Assam in 1981 and Jammu and Kashmir in 1991, but this is the first time that the 2027 exercise has been disrupted.

In further updates, The first phase of Census 2027 (house listing) in Manipur was scheduled from September 1 to 30. The self-enumeration facility was set to be available from August 17 to 31. Amid protests and training of census workers being disrupted by locals, self-enumeration for house listing was also not started.

On top of that, The decision came on a day the Manipur high court directed that the house-listing exercise be withheld, pending further notification from the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, amid petitions seeking implementation of NRC before the census.
Since August 16, Manipur has been roiled by protests by Naga and Meitei organisations that demanded an NRC before the census. The Kuki-Zo communities are opposed to the move.

title: Congress to hold massive protests over FIR against Rahul Gandhi: KC Venugopal
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Congress revealed “massive protest marches” on Monday evening over a first information report (FIR) registered against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in Uttarakhand, intensifying the political battle over some people “purifying” the Ramlila ground at Haldwani after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a public meeting there.

Adding to this, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi addressing a press conference at the AICC headquarters on Saturday (HT Photo/Sanchit Khanna) The FIR was registered by the Haldwani police on Sunday, a day after Gandhi addressed a press conference in New Delhi to demand that Prime Minister Narendra Modi order an FIR against those involved in the “purification” of the Ramlila ground at Haldwani.
Meanwhile, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal shared the FIR against Rahul Gandhi was a “shameless weaponisation of the state machinery” to target the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

Notably, Venugopal told the party’s state and district units to hold protest marches at the state and district headquarters on Monday evening to register their “vehement condemnation of this vendetta politics and to demand immediate legal action against the guilty BJP workers in Uttarakhand”.

As per the latest buzz, The FIR, registered on a complaint by Amit Kumar, a member of Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas, accused Gandhi of offences under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and sections 196 (promoting enmity between classes) and 299 (malicious acts to outrage religious feelings) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The FIR shared Gandhi wrongly described the cleaning and havan ritual as an act of “untouchability” and an atrocity against the Scheduled Caste community without verifying the facts.

In further updates, Venugopal shared the party’s fight against those who attack the values of social justice enshrined in the Constitution should continue and asked all party leaders at the state and district levels to participate in the protests.

On top of that, He shared party units should ensure the maximum mobilisation and media dissemination “to send an unyielding message: the Indian National Congress will not be intimidated by state-sponsored witch-hunts and will fight relentlessly for social justice, constitutional equality, and the dignity of every citizen.”

“The BJP’s blatant defence of this casteist behaviour and its shameless weaponisation of the state machinery to target the Leader of the Opposition unequivocally proves that they are the biggest perpetrators or protectors of social injustice today. They have demonstrated that they will deploy the entire might of the state to suppress anyone who dares to speak out against caste-based discrimination and Dalit atrocities,” he shared.

title: Delhi Police tells SC it ‘no longer wishes to pursue’ 13 FIRs from NEET protests in July
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
Delhi Police on Monday evening told the Supreme Court that it "no longer wishes to pursue" 13 FIRs from the Cockroach Janta Party-led NEET protests in July, invoking Article 142 over the matter.

Adding to this, Abhijeet Dipke's CJP had led a student protest movement from Delhi's Jantar Mantar against the NEET paper leak, which eventually resulted in the resignation of ex-education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. (ANI) Delhi Police shared that the Centre, on July 25, 2026, decided to move away from prosecuting the broader protest FIRs, which cover rioting, attempt to murder, and property damage, and instead decided to narrow its focus.

Meanwhile, In its application, filed on behalf of the Union government, the police shared that they would not register any further FIRs in connection with the protests between July 20 and July 25. The plea is likely to come up before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Tuesday.

Notably, The move comes days before the proposed September 5 protest march revealed by the CJP from India Gate to the Delhi Police headquarters, with withdrawal of FIRs against student protesters being one of the principal demands of the group.

As per the latest buzz, The Supreme Court earlier on Monday declined to interfere with the proposed march, leaving the question of law-and-order arrangements to the Centre and Delhi government. The court, however, expressed confidence that all stakeholders would act peacefully and within the legal framework.
In further updates, The Delhi Police told Supreme Court that a single fresh FIR would be filed against against 2,873 persons who were prima facie found to have “serious criminal antecedents.”

On top of that, The application shared the new FIR would be in conformity with the court’s clarification on “criminal antecedents” in its previous order. “The investigation is required to ascertain their role, if any, in the commission of offences relating to bodily harm or destruction of property at the shared protests,” it shared.

The Delhi Police shared that their probe will focus only on people's role in violence and damage, informing the top court that remaining protesters booked across the 13 FIRs are “effectively let off.”

title: This actor cycled 140 km daily to acting school, survived on ₹18 and Frooti-biscuit lunches, then won National Award
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Rajkummar Rao is one of the most critically acclaimed actors in the country. As he turns 42 on Monday, we look back at his journey from struggling to make ends meet in Mumbai to establishing himself as one of the most sought-after actors in the Hindi movie industry.

Adding to this, Rajkummar Rao in a still from Prahaar. 'Would cycle for 140 kms' In an interaction with Ranveer Allahbadia in 2024, Rajkummar shared that he wanted to become an star from his school days and was involved in theatre. It was his mother who recognised his passion and encouraged him to pursue acting.

Meanwhile, Rajkummar, who hails from Gurugram, recalled that at the age of 18, he would cycle 70 km each way from Gurugram to Delhi every day to attend acting school at the Sri Ram Centre. He would often listen to songs such as “Lakshya Ko Har Haal Me Pana Hai” and “Papa Kahte Hain” on his walkman during the journey. The star shared that though it might sound romantic, but it was his reality at that time and he didn't mind it.

Notably, Rajkummar got his first break in Dibakar Banerjee's Love Sex Aur Dhokha. The star, however, wasn't paid well for the movie and collected ₹ 11,000 for it. He recalled that the amount lasted him for a month. However, the star admitted that even during those difficult financial times, he made sure he didn't fall into the 'trap' of taking up projects solely for money.

As per the latest buzz, The darkest phase came when Rajkummar was struggling in Mumbai and did not have enough money to buy himself a meal. He shared, “The most difficult time was facing financial difficulty and getting no work. My mother supported me a lot and when I would run out of money, she would arrange it and send. I remember once I was left with only ₹ 18 in my account and that too in a city like Mumbai. I used to spend very frugally. We three used to live in one flat and I used to skip lunch and have one Parle G and Frooti for lunch. My lunch would cost me ₹ 4 at the time.”

In further updates, This was the time when Rajkummar's FTII batchmates came to his help. He shared, “Now, the day I was left with only ₹ 18, I was thinking what will I do? We have a FTII (Movie and Television Institute of India) committee in Mumbai. A lot of our seniors and juniors live here. So, you can ring anybody and ask them what are they having for dinner and if you can come.”

On top of that, After Love Sex Aur Dhokha, Rajkummar starred in critically acclaimed films such as Gangs of Wasseypur 2, Kai Po Che!, Queen, Shaitaan, Aligarh and Shahid,which made him win the Best Star National Award. While several of Rajkummar's films did not emerge as major box-office successes, his performances were widely appreciated by critics and audiences. He was last seen in Toaster with Sanya Malhotra.

Rajkummar will next be seen in Prahaar: The Ujjwal Nikam Story, a biographical courtroom drama based on the life and career of renowned public prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam. The movie is directed by Avinash Arun and produced by Dinesh Vijan under Maddock Films. It also stars Wamiqa Gabbi, Jaideep Ahlawat, Sikander Kher, Ashish Vidyarthi, Lalit Prabhakar and Ritvik Sahore. The movie explores some of the landmark cases associated with Nikam, including the trial of 26/11 Mumbai terror attack accused Ajmal Kasab.

title: Daayra trailer out: Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran face off on opposite sides of justice in Meghna Gulzar’s thriller
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Inspired by true events, Daayra unfolds in the aftermath of a crime that grips the nation sparking widespread outrage, while setting a series of events and 2 investigations in motion. As the search for answers deepens, two senior police officers, played by Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran, find themselves navigating the same system through different approaches to duty and justice, on opposing sides of a case that challenges the very idea of right and wrong.

Adding to this, Rooted in realism, the trailer steadily builds tension as new revelations shift the way we see the case. Its sharp, thought-provoking dialogues raise difficult questions on truth and justice. At the same time, Daayra looks beyond the crime itself to explore public perception and the narratives that emerge. At its heart, Daayra asks questions that have no easy answers: How quickly can a narrative become a verdict? When everyone has an opinion, who gets to decide what justice looks like? And when we are only spectators, what do we choose to believe?

Meanwhile, The trailer also offers glimpses of the wider ensemble, with powerful performances by Jitendra Joshi, Kshitee Jog, Kanwaljeet Singh, Sandeep Kulkarni and Trupti Khamkar. Alongside Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran, they bring added emotional depth to a story shaped by conflicting perspectives, difficult choices and the consequences of decisions made.

Notably, Star Kareena Kapoor Khan shared, “What I loved about working with Meghna is that she makes you question everything you think you know about a character. There’s so much thought behind every detail, but she never takes away your instinct as an star. Playing DCP Ajooni Kohli stayed with me… because she pushed me into a space I hadn’t really explored before, and at this stage in my career, that’s always exciting. And then to have Prithviraj opposite me was such a pleasure. He’s an incredibly intelligent star… very present, very instinctive… and there was an ease to working together that I really enjoyed. This was one of those films where the people you’re surrounded by make the experience that much richer.”

As per the latest buzz, Star Prithviraj Sukumaran shared, “What drew me to DCP Raman Kumar was the complexity beneath his composed exterior and the questions he finds himself grappling with during the investigation. What I admire is how the movie maintains that objectivity right till the very end, allowing the audience to form their own perspective. Meghna Gulzar is a filmmaker whose craft I have closely followed, and Daayra gave me the opportunity to work with her. It was a rewarding experience, and working with Kareena made the journey even more special. I hope the audience connects with the world we have created, a story that is gripping and deeply human”

In further updates, Director Meghna Gulzar shared, " Daayra doesn’t sit comfortably in black and white. It explores the grey and dismantles it. As a filmmaker, that grey space is always challenging, and yet compelling – where characters make choices, live with them, and the audience is left to engage with what unfolds. The main protagonists of Daayra are brought to life with towering performances by Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran. I’m grateful that I got this dynamic combination of actors, along with an exceptional ensemble cast, to explore the delicate lines of law and justice that traverse the story of Daayra . I am very excited to share this world of grey with the audience and welcome them into it!"

On top of that, Amrita Pandey, CEO, Junglee Pictures, shared, “At Junglee Pictures, we have always gravitated towards stories that come from the world around us, particularly those inspired by true events or real experiences. Daayra has been a story we have developed closely with our writers and Meghna, and it is a movie that feels deeply relevant to the times we live in, while approaching its subject with the sensitivity it deserves. It is also a powerful crime thriller, driven by conflict, moral dilemmas, difficult choices and two very strong points of view. To have powerhouse performers like Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran bring these characters to life makes it even more exciting. Daayra also marks our first co-production with PEN Studios, and we are delighted to be on this journey with them. For our team, it is wonderful to be working with Meghna for the third time after Talvar and Raazi. We have loved making this movie and hope audiences connect with it as deeply as we have.”

Dr. Jayantilal Gada, CMD, Pen Studios shared, "Cinema can entertain, but it can also ask the right questions. Daayra belongs to the latter, and that is what makes this story particularly special to us. Meghna Gulzar is a filmmaker who has consistently created cinema that makes you think, and her ability to tell a story with depth, sensitivity and restraint is truly remarkable. Bringing together two celebrated actors like Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran adds another compelling dimension to the movie, with both actors bringing immense conviction and intensity to their roles. It has also been wonderful to collaborate with a content-first studio like Junglee Pictures, whose vision and commitment to meaningful storytelling align closely with ours. We hope Daayra not only grips audiences but also stays with them, leaving them with questions and conversations long after they leave the theatre.”

title: Shalini Pandey speaks out against ‘deeply disturbing’ AI video featuring her: ‘I strongly condemn this kind of abuse’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Shalini Pandey has become the latest star to fall prey to the growing menace of deepfake videos. However, she is taking swift action to address the issue. She has issued a clarification, categorically stating that she has no involvement with the video.

Adding to this, Shalini Pandey rolled out a statement addressing an AI video of her. Shalini's statement Taking to her Instagram account on Monday, Shalini shared a note which read, “I want to address a fake AI-generated video of me that is currently being circulated online. The video is completely fabricated and does not depict me. It is deeply disturbing to see technology being misused in this way to target and harm individuals, especially women.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shalini Pandey (@shalzp)

Notably, She added, “I strongly condemn this kind of abuse and believe this kind of misuse of technology should never be normalised. If you come across this video, please do not share, forward, download, or engage with it. Instead, please report it immediately. I request everyone to responsible and mindful, and help stop its circulation rather than giving it further reach. Thankyou!”

As per the latest buzz, In the past, many Indian celebrities have been the subject of deepfakes, including Rashmika Mandanna, Alia Bhatt, Deepika Padukone, Katrina Kaif, Aamir Khan, Ranveer Singh, and Sachin Tendulkar.

In further updates, Earlier this month, Mrunal Thakur took a stand against it and warned those who are creating deepfakes of her. Calling out the growing misuse of AI-generated content, the star described such acts as “illegal and unacceptable” and stressed that people should be held accountable for using someone else's identity without permission.

On top of that, She made it clear that such actions would not be tolerated and wrote, “Creating or sharing deepfake content using my likeness is illegal and unacceptable. Consider this your formal notice to stop immediately. Any further misuse of my identity will result in legal action..”

Shalini made her acting debut in the 2017 hit Arjun Reddy with Vijay Deverakonda . The movie became a major smash hit and turned her into a recognized name. She went on to appear in movies like Mahanati (2018), Jayeshbhai Jordaar (2022), and Maharaj (2024). Shalini made her Hindi debut in Yash Raj Films' Jayeshbhai Jordaar (2022) with Ranveer Singh. She also starred in Netflix's Maharaj (2024), and pivotal parts in the show Dabba Cartel and the Tamil movie Idly Kadai, both of which rolled out last year.

title: Centre asks SC to quash FIRs on NEET protesters; CJP's Dipke reacts with Ambedkar book, Saurav Das posts selfie
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Central government on Monday moved an application in the Supreme Court, seeking to quash the FIRs filed by the police against protesters led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, along with other states.

Adding to this, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacted to the development with a post on the social media platform X. (X/ Abhijeet Dipke) The FIRs were filed over allegations of violence during the NEET paper leak protests in Delhi and other states. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leader Saurav Das reacted to the development with posts on the social media platform X.

Meanwhile, Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta mentioned the plea before a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. He shared that the Centre seeks the top court to invoke its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to quash FIRs against protesters.
Notably, The Supreme Court will take up the case on Tuesday.
As per the latest buzz, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacted to the Centre moving to quash FIRs against NEET protesters with a photo holding a book by Dr BR Ambedkar.
In further updates, Dipke did not write anything in the post. He held the book up to the camera so that Dr Ambedkar's photo would be visible.
On top of that, Ambedkar imagery was a vital part of the CJP-led protest. When Dipke arrived in India back in June, he exited the airport in Delhi holding a book by India's first law minister.
Apart from Dipke, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das also reacted to the development with a cheeky selfie.

title: Rajkumar Santoshi disagrees with Shabana Azmi claiming that Batwara 1947 failed due to Sunny Deol playing Muslim
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
The filmmaker defended Sunny’s character and insisted that audiences should look at the intent behind a story rather than the faith of a character.

Adding to this, Santoshi pointed to Amitabh Bachchan’s portrayal of Muslim characters in several films as an example of how cinema has historically embraced characters from different faiths. He shared, “It makes no sense to me. Amitabh Bachchan played a Muslim hero in Coolie (1983). So many of Manmohan Desai’s films had Muslim heroes. Are we at a point where we cannot accept a hero from the other community? We are sensible, good people, educated people. How are they saying there’s a big mistake in the movie?”

Meanwhile, The filmmaker further expressed concern over what he described as a decline in tolerance and inclusivity. Emphasising that the intent behind a movie should be considered, Santoshi shared, “We have become far less tolerant and inclusive as a people. You should look at the filmmaker’s intent and what the writer wants to say.”

Notably, Santoshi also spoke about his own religious beliefs while stressing that his approach is not against any faith. He shared, “I’m a Hindu. I go to the temple. My son’s name is Ram. I am not against any faith. But I want to take the best of every faith. Whatever the saints have tried to say about faith, it is always about equality. Hinduism has always been about inclusiveness, not exclusion.”

As per the latest buzz, His comments come after Shabana Azmi expressed surprise over the theatrical performance of Batwara 1947 . In conversation with Zoom, the veteran star had suggested that Sunny Deol’s casting as a Muslim character could have been a factor behind the movie’s reception.

In further updates, Azmi shared, “The thing is that you cannot accept Sunny Deol as a Muslim. In Coolie and in many other films, Amitabh Bachchan very comfortably played Muslim characters. In Deewaar , he put 786, and that was accepted. So how do we understand this? Are they creating an environment where such decisions are being taken on purpose? I am not able to understand.”

On top of that, She further shared, “I am surprised at how people are reacting to it. Even the ones who watched the movie think Sunny Deol is playing a Pakistani. He is not. It is simply not registering in their heads. Even Bushra Ahmed (Pakistani star) objected to the movie’s language. She shared the Punjabi dialect used by the villain is not right. If both religions are not liking the movie, it means it is something which is pure and beautiful,” she added.

With Santoshi now weighing in on the debate, the discussion around Batwara 1947 has extended beyond its ticket-window performance to questions about representation, religious identity and the freedom to portray characters from different communities in mainstream Hindi cinema.

title: Sonali Kulkarni on playing Salman Khan's mother in Bharat despite being 9 years younger: ‘Was paid well’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sonali Kulkarni is nine years younger than Salman Khan , but she played his mother in Ali Abbas Zafar'ss movie Bharat . Sonali is 51, while Salman is 60 years old. In a recent interaction, Sonali opened up about her decision to play a much older character in the movie.

Adding to this, Sonali Kulkarni played Salman Khan's mother in Bharat. 'A lot of convincing' In conversation with SCREEN, she admitted that during the casting process, she felt she “can’t be playing this role”. However, Ali Abbas Zafar and casting director Mukesh Chhabra were “very sure” about her casting and convinced her to take up the role. They argued that her character was important because of the emphasis placed on the flashback sequences.

Meanwhile, She shared, “The flashback meant everything to that movie. That’s how Bharat gets his name and reacts to situations. No director or casting director would like to fit in a wrong person somewhere. That would be a failure on their part also. So, I tried to understand that. So, I took it up as a challenge.”

Notably, Sonali Kulkarni shared that it still took “a lot of convincing” on both their parts. She also admitted that it was her 'temptation' to meet Salman Khan that encouraged her to play the role. Speaking about her experience of working with the superstar, she shared, “We bonded very well on the sets of Bharat. One can learn from him to treat people well. He was ever gracious. And he scored a point when he gave me his cycle to ride."
As per the latest buzz, Sonali also added the role paid her “really well”, she did her maximum scenes with the child artiste who played the young Salman in the movie.

In further updates, The movie is directed and co-written by Ali Abbas Zafar. It stars Salman Khan, Katrina Kaif, Sunil Grover, Jackie Shroff, Disha Patani and Tabu. The movie received positive reviews from critics and audiences. It was also a box-office success and was among the highest-grossing films of 2019. It grossed ₹ 325.58 crore rupees during its lifetime theatrical run.

On top of that, Salman Khan has Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, earlier titled Battle of Galwan, in the pipeline. Directed by Apoorva Lakhia, the movie also stars Chitrangda Singh and is backed by Salman Khan Films. A new poster rolled out in July indicated that the movie remains slated for a 2026 rollout, although an exact theatrical date has not been revealed.

Salman is also set to star in the yet-to-be-titled SVC63, directed by Vamshi Paidipally. The movie marks his collaboration with South Indian star Nayanthara, while Anil Kapoor is also part of the cast. The action drama is currently expected to rollout on Eid in 2027.

title: Daayra trailer: Kareena Kapoor probes Prithviraj's encounter killings as Meghna Gulzar explores law vs justice
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Kareena Kapoor will soon be back on the big screen. The makers of her soon-to-release movie Daayra unveiled the movie's trailer on Monday. The Meghna Gulzar directorial also stars Prithviraj Sukumaran. The movie is inspired by true events and explores the complex relationship between crime, justice and punishment.

Adding to this, Daayra stars Prithviraj Sukumaran and Kareena Kapoor Khan. Daayra trailer Daayra is a crime thriller that stars Kareena and Prithviraj as cops, DCP Ajooni Kohli and DCP Raman Kumar. The movie is inspired by true events and sees Prithviraj's character dealing with a gang rape case. The trailer opens with a distressed woman looking for her daughter. Other glimpses show Prithviraj taking the accused juveniles to an isolated location and shooting them, showing it as an encounter later.

Meanwhile, Kareena then enters the frame and questions Prithviraj about three other encounters he carried out in the past in self-defence. This sets Kareena's investigation into motion as she probes the encounter and Prithviraj's fight against the criminals accused of committing the heinous crime of gang rape.

Notably, The investigation is done, crime scene is recreated, and Prithviraj is warned. However, he remains unbothered, saying, "Again a family has lost their daughter." Kareena points out that one of the accused was going to turn 17.

As per the latest buzz, Towards the end of the trailer, Kareena says that she works within the boundaries of the law. Prithviraj, however, argues against this, questioning how a juvenile who can commit such a heinous crime can be protected by the Juvenile Protection Law. The trailer leaves the audience with the question of whether justice can always be served within the boundaries of the law.

In further updates, Daayra is co-written and directed by Meghna Gulzar and produced by Junglee Pictures and Pen Studios. It stars Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran in the lead roles. The movie marks the first on-screen collaboration between the two actors. It is scheduled to rollout in theatres on September 18.

On top of that, In an earlier interaction, Meghna's father and lyricist Gulzar had verified that the movie has no songs. With Daayra, Kareena will return to the big screen after a gap of two years. She was last seen in Ajay Devgn and Rohit Shetty's Singham Again in 2024. This is Kareena's first collaboration with Meghna Gulzar.

Filmmaker Meghna Gulzar has carved a niche for herself by bringing compelling real-life stories and issues to the big screen, often exploring them with nuance and sensitivity. Her filmography includes Talvar, inspired by the Aarushi-Hemraj murder case, Chhapaak, which brought acid attack survivor Laxmi Agarwal's extraordinary journey to the screen, and Sam Bahadur, a biographical drama on Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw.

title: 'Big star-led films don't speak to me,' says Paatal Lok, Kohrra creator Sudip Sharma: 'I don't even watch them'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Filmmaker-writer Sudip Sharma , who has contributed as a writer to films such as NH10 and Udta Punjab , says he has no immediate plans to direct a feature movie for the big screen as he finds himself more drawn to the long-form series format. Sharma most of late contributed as a writer on Anurag Kashyap's movie Bandar.

Adding to this, Sudip Sharma talks about his preference for shows over films. Sudip Sharma on star-led commercial films I don't know what kind of movie to direct right now. There is a lot of churn that is happening, and the kind of films that are mostly getting made are not the kind of films that inherently interest me, the writer-director told PTI in an interview.

Meanwhile, Best known for OTT titles like Paatal Lok and Kohrra, the filmmaker shared the streaming shows give him a broader canvas to tell stories on his own terms -- offering far more creative liberty than filmmaking does currently.

Notably, “I enjoy long-form storytelling; there is something very satisfying about it as a writer and as a creator, even more so than as a director. It is very satisfying as a writer-creator because of the kind of places you can go, the kind of themes, and the lives you can dive into. Somehow, I find movie restrictive in that sense right now. It might change,” he added.
As per the latest buzz, Besides, the 43-year-old filmmaker does not see himself as the right fit for making star-driven films, which currently dominate Hindi cinema.

In further updates, “Those kinds of star vehicles don't necessarily speak to me. I don't even watch them. I don't think I am the right person to make them. Nothing against those films. Some of those are very successful films, and we need those films to be able to make these because that's how the industry sort of funnels it back in,” he shared.

On top of that, “I don't think I am the right person for those kinds of films. I don't want to do it just because it's a big project or that's how it should be. Not that they have been offered to me, but the idea doesn't excite me,” he added.
Sharma, however, shared there are no immediate plans to direct a feature movie and that he has already begun work on an OTT show.

title: India's most profitable film of 2026 earned 2000% profit: How a ₹2 crore film beat Dhurandhar, Awarapan 2, Toxic, Peddi
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

2026 may not have been a red-letter year for Indian cinema at the ticket-window, but it has seen some massive individual successes across languages. Be it Dhurandhar the Revenge, Jana Nayagan, or Awarapan 2 , films have broken through in various genres and across scales and budgets to script success. But none of these is the biggest hit of the year from India. That record belongs to a spiritual movie with no star, a small budget, and hardly any promotion. And yet, it has collected more than 20x its production budget.

Adding to this, A still from the biggest box-office hit from India this year. India’s most profitable movie of 2026 The devotional drama Hanuman Ansh , about the life and legacy of spiritual leader Neem Karoli Baba, is the biggest box-office hit in Indian cinema this year, earning a staggering 2000% profit and already making 21x its budget on the back of strong word-of-mouth. Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, Hanuman Ansh features an ensemble cast, with Chandan Anand and Shobhinav Satyaa in the lead roles. The movie was made on a shoestring budget of ₹ 2 crore rupees and rolled out in theatres without much fanfare on August 7. It failed to gain traction initially and was written off as a box-office failure in its first week.

Meanwhile, However, Hanuman Ansh began to generate enough buzz by the second weekend to force exhibitors to increase their shows. This led to a huge surge in its collections. The movie collected just ₹ 60 lakh in its opening weekend. This figure jumped to a staggering ₹ 28 crore rupees in its fourth weekend. Hanuman Ansh has now collected over ₹ 42 crore rupees net in India and is heading towards the ₹ 50-crore rupees mark. Industry insiders say that given its pace, a ₹ 100-crore rupees lifetime run is not unfathomable. If it achieves that, it will become one of the most profitable Indian films of all time.

Notably, Hanuman Ansh currently has a 2000% profit with its ticket-window earnings. Industry insiders say this could go up to 5000% by the time the movie ends its run. In comparison, Dhurandhar 2 had a 1000% profit due to its relatively bigger budget of around ₹ 125 crore rupees. Similarly, Awarapan 2 has made a profit of around 450% over its ₹ 30-crore rupees budget with its box-office collections alone.

As per the latest buzz, The movie traces the life of Lakshman Das and how he found spiritualism, transforming into Neem Karoli Baba. It follows the spiritual leader's journey from age 13 to the point where he came to be loved and revered. The movie's writer-director is a doctor-turned-filmmaker. It is produced by Swambhu Media Network Pvt. Ltd., Ragini S., Namrata G. S., and Anupriya A. Nagar. Hanuman Ansh is currently running in theatres.

In further updates, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. title: EXCLUSIVE: CBFC cuts 35 seconds of intimate scenes in Mirzapur The Movie; mutes cuss words in 4 places, replaces abuses in 6 places
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The CBFC asked for several cuts before handing over the censor certificate to the makers. To begin with, cuss words were muted at 4 places, while at 6 places, the abuses were replaced with ‘appropriate’ words. The dialogue ‘Galey se lag gar’ was also modified.

Adding to this, In the first half of the movie, a word was replaced with ' kamar '. Meanwhile, in the post-interval part, the word ' lanth ', which means idiot, was asked to be modified. A caste reference was also asked to be modified.

Meanwhile, As for the visual cuts, the makers were asked to reduce intimate scenes by 50% through suitable modifications in visuals and sound. This was done in two scenes, one in first half and one in the second half. As a result, 35 seconds of intimate scenes were deleted.

Notably, Interestingly, not a single violent and gory scene was censored by the CBFC. Once these changes were made, the censor certificate was given to the makers of Mirzapur The Movie . The length of the movie, as mentioned on the certificate, is 197.19 minutes. In other words, it is 3 hours, 17 minutes and 19 seconds long.

As per the latest buzz, The censor certificate also mentions that Mirzapur The Movie was passed by the Revising Committee of the CBFC. Usually, the Examining Committee is the first to view the movie, and when it asks for several modifications, the makers can approach the RC. The Revising Committee then reviews the movie and makes the final call on the certification and suggested modifications.

title: Mirzapur the Movie cleared by CBFC with 'hardly any modifications', retains 'raw, unfiltered essence': Source
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The movie adaptation of Mirzapur , the popular web series, is set for rollout this week. The movie, which tells the origin story of the Pandit brothers’ feud with Kaleen Bhaiya, releases in theatres this Friday. Ahead of its rollout, the movie has finally secured a certificate from the Central Board for Movie Certification ( CBFC ). And sources say that the violent crime drama has managed to avoid the censor’s scissors.

Adding to this, Mirzapur The Movie: Divyenndu returns as Munna Tripathi. Mirzapur: The Movie cleared by CBFC The movie stars Pankaj Tripathi , Ali Fazal, Divyenndu, and Jitendra Kumar in the lead roles, and tells the story of how Guddu and Bablu Pandit stood up against Kaleen Bhaiya’s empire in the titular town. According to a source close to the movie, Mirzapur The Movie has been certified by the CBFC with 'hardly any modifications'. "This means audiences will get to experience the much-awaited theatrical adaptation exactly the way the makers intended it to be seen, retaining its raw, unfiltered essence on the big screen," says the source. Some reports had claimed that 35 seconds of footage had been cut from the movie, but the source says that there are no cuts and very few modifications in the movie.
Meanwhile, Mirzapur, the show, is known for its gritty realism and shocking violence. The movie aims to bring the same essence to theatres on a grander scale.

Notably, Talking about what is new in the movie, Pankaj Tripathi told HT last month that the communal viewing experience will change how people see Mirzapur. “Whenever a performance or art form is experienced communally, the impact changes entirely. Enjoying it in a group creates a unique, shared experience. So, while Mirzapur used to be a "leave me alone” kind of watch, it’s now in "party mode.” The world is the same, the characters are the same, but the story is new, and the experience is much grander,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, The makers have rolled out the trailer of Mirzapur: The Movie, which continues from the world of Season 1, bringing together some of the franchise's most beloved and iconic characters, including Kaleen Bhaiya, Munna Bhaiya and Guddu Pandit. Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, Divyendu, and Rasika Dugal are all returning. The character of Bablu Pandit, originally played by Vikrant Massey in the series, will be portrayed by Jitendra Kumar in the movie. The movie also stars Ravi Kishan in a brand-new role.

title: Chandrachur Singh files FIR over alleged forgery of grandfather’s will, accuses family members
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Chandrachur claimed his grandfather was seriously ill at the time and unable to sign the documents. He also alleged that properties mentioned in the disputed will were later sold.

Adding to this, The complaint was registered at Rorawar police station in Aligarh on Friday. Singh has alleged that the signature of his grandfather, Thakur Harender Pal Singh, was forged on a will in 1997, at a time when his grandfather was seriously unwell and, according to the star, was not in a condition to sign legal documents.

Meanwhile, Singh has accused his uncle Ganga Singh and other relatives of being involved in the alleged forgery. He claimed that the disputed document resulted in his father, Captain Baldev Singh, being deprived of his share of the family inheritance.

In further updates, The family dispute had come into the public domain last year when Gaytri Devi denied the allegations against her. She had accused Chandrachur Singh of attempting to falsely implicate her and maintained that the will was genuine.
On top of that, Singh’s father, Captain Baldev Singh, was a former Congress MLA from Aligarh city and died a few years ago.
The police have now registered a case and begun investigating the allegations. The claims made by Chandrachur Singh in the FIR are allegations at this stage and have not yet been established.

title: 'Everyone gone, now no hope': Sonam Wangchuk says CJP leaders wanted to end protest after July 20 crackdown
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Sonam Wangchuk has opened up that leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were looking for a way to end their protest after a police crackdown at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 20, when the movement's stage was dismantled and many protesters left the site.

Adding to this, Activist Sonam Wangchuk, with his wife Gitanjali J Angmo, visits Rajghat to pay tributes to Mahatma Gandhi. (PTI) Wangchuk, in conversation with Prakhar Gupta on the PGX podcast, shared CJP's leadership was deeply demoralised after the action and had asked him to help craft a message encouraging protesters to leave Jantar Mantar and return home.
Meanwhile, “Now everyone has gone, our stage has also been broken, now there is no hope,” Wangchuk recalled the CJP leadership telling him after the July 20 action.
Notably, According to Wangchuk , the organisers wanted him to post a message telling protesters that they were tired and should take a break.
As per the latest buzz, “They wanted me to post something saying that you need a good rest now, go sleep at home, don't stay at Jantar Mantar, we can see tomorrow what to do,” he shared.
In further updates, Wangchuk shared he did write such a message, although it was ultimately not posted.

On top of that, The July 20 crackdown came after a large mobilisation around the protest. Wangchuk shared the immediate aftermath left the CJP leadership believing that the movement had effectively collapsed.
“Everyone thought that whatever one or two lakh people had come, they had all left that night, so everything was over,” he shared.

Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday declared that the BJP , after being in power for years and having control over the country’s central investigative agencies, had begun to believe that it had become bigger than its ideological mentor, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). He was addressing a press conference in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.

Adding to this, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat. (PTI/AFP) The activist referred to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat ’s address at a conference in New York titled ‘One World One Humanity’, where he remarked that a Hindu who believed that India should have no Muslims was not truly a Hindu.
Meanwhile, “I have been saying from the beginning that BJP leaders need to start heeding Mohan Bhagwat’s advice,” the CJP founder shared.

Notably, Taking a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Dipke shared the BJP leadership had failed to follow Bhagwat’s message of inclusivity. “Bhagwat had earlier shared that Gen Z protesters should not be called anti-national, but soon after that, Modi came up with the term ‘Dimaagi Naxal’,” he shared. “It was clear that he was not listening to Bhagwat. If you do not want to listen to us, at least listen to your mentor, the RSS. You are in government because of them.”

As per the latest buzz, Talking about the CJP’s scheduled protest in New Delhi on September 5, Dipke shared the protesters would assemble at India Gate and march towards the police headquarters. “It will be a peaceful march, and I believe it will be bigger than the Jantar Mantar protest,” he shared.

In further updates, The activist shared the protest was being revived over two demands—withdrawal of FIRs registered against protesting students and compensation for the families of those who died by suicide after the NEET paper leaks. “These demands were agreed to by the union ministers we spoke with after Jantar Mantar,” he shared. “But despite repeated attempts to engage with the government, no resolution has been reached. We have now started believing that the government is deliberately adopting delaying tactics, leaving us with no option but to resume our protest.”

On top of that, Asked whether he was concerned about a fresh FIR against him for the ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign, Dipke shared he was unfazed. “Let them file an FIR,” he shared. “This will not be the first and it will not be the last. It does not bother me. When I returned from the US, I had already made up my mind that I might end up in jail one day.”

The activist also questioned the credibility of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls being undertaken by the Election Commission of India after 3,400 filled SIR forms were found in the possession of a BJP worker in Navi Mumbai.

title: Arshad Warsi reveals Jaya Bachchan warned wife Maria about marrying an actor: ‘We hang out with good-looking people'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Arshad Warsi of late recalled an advice his wife, Maria Goretti, received from Jaya Bachchan before she got married to him. The Munna Bhai MBBS star remembered how Jaya warned Maria about the challenges of marrying an star.

Adding to this, Arshad Warsi recalls Jaya Bachchan's advice. 'Most difficult things to do in life is to marry an star' A legendary star in her own right, Jaya Bachchan has been married to the country's megastar Amitabh Bachchan for more than five decades. This is why she understands the sacrifices and challenges that come with sharing a life with an star. In conversation with Filmigyan, Arshad shared that Jaya spoke to Maria from her own experience.

Meanwhile, He shared, “Jaya is a very intelligent woman. She told me, she says, ‘It is one of the most difficult things to do in life, is to marry an star.’ I wouldn’t say star ki fitrat hai, but unfortunately, you’re always put in situations where you are hanging with very interesting people, very good-looking people."

Notably, He added, "Jaya ji actually shared, when Maria and I were getting married, that one of the most difficult things to do in life is to marry an star. She told us, ‘Are you ready for it?’ That’s the reason why, because your job makes you do things that are not normal for a normal couple. So then you have to cross that barrier and still be with that person. So your love has to be beyond normal people’s love and attention."

As per the latest buzz, Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan met on the sets of the movie Guddi in 1971. However, they grew closer while filming Ek Nazar in 1972. After the success of Zanjeer in 1973, they tied the knot in the same year. The couple went on to welcome two children, daughter Shweta Bachchan and son Abhishek Bachchan. They have three grandchildren — Navya Naveli Nanda, Agastya Nanda and Aaradhya Bachchan.

In further updates, In a 2025 interview with Mojo Story, Jaya shared her views on marriage. She shared, “I have not asked him. He might say that ‘biggest mistake of my life’, but I don’t want to hear that. Do you have to dig into old wounds? I have been married for the last 52 years to the same man. Isse jada pyaar main nahin kar sakti hoon. (I can't love more than that). It will sound outdated for me to say that you shouldn’t get married… It was love at first sight.”

title: Rahul Roy didn't know if he would be able to walk again after brain stroke, reveals his routine: ‘I have 8 medicines’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Rahul Roy ’s life changed in a matter of hours when he suffered a brain stroke in 2020. The Aashiqui star, who became one of the biggest stars of the early 1990s and later won the first season of Bigg Boss , has now opened up about the difficult period that followed. He says the experience forced him to look at life differently. He is now slowly getting back to work and will be seen in the soon-to-release series Super Badshah.

Adding to this, Rahul Roy recalls terrifying brain stroke: ‘I didn’t know if I would be able to walk or talk again’. The stroke that changed everything Rahul suffered a cerebrovascular stroke in November 2020 while shooting for LAC – Live The Battle in Kargil. He was first taken to Srinagar and was later brought to Mumbai, where he was admitted to Nanavati Hospital and spent time in the ICU. The star has spoken about how frightening those initial days were, particularly because he had no idea what his recovery would look like.

Meanwhile, In conversation with Free Press Journal, he shared, “The only thing I was sceptical about was my speech problem because of the brain stroke which I had in 2020 when I was shooting in Kargil. But Karanvir was supportive throughout. After my brain stroke, I didn't even know if I would be able to walk or talk again.”

Notably, Recovery was not something that happened overnight. Roy had to gradually work his way back, with his family supporting him through the process. One of the biggest changes Roy made after the stroke was to his lifestyle. He was previously a heavy smoker and ate non-vegetarian food, but has since completely changed his diet. His mornings now also come with a strict medication routine. He added, “Every day after breakfast, I have 8 medicines. But things are much better now than before”.

As per the latest buzz, Rahul Roy shot to fame with Aashiqui in 1990, his debut movie with Mahesh Bhatt , in which he starred opposite Anu Aggarwal. The movie turned him into an overnight sensation and established him as one of the most recognisable faces of that generation. He later appeared in films such as Junoon and eventually entered reality television, winning the first season of Bigg Boss in 2007 against Carol Gracias and taking home the ₹ 1 crore rupees prize.

In further updates, His career has gone through several ups and downs since then. His last major movie appearance was in Kanu Behl’s psychological drama Agra, which rolled out in November 2025. He will feature in Kuku TV’s Super Badshah, where he plays an underworld don alongside Karanvir Bohra .

title: Sonam Wangchuk REACTS to Aamir Khan’s 3 Idiots claim: “Maybe he was so deeply into his Ghajini character that he forgot meeting me”
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Aamir Khan had claimed that he had never met Sonam Wangchuk before making 3 Idiots.

Adding to this, “He shared we had never met. Then some videos emerged in which he was watching my speech in his Ghajini outfit. As he was in the Ghajini look, maybe he would have suffered short-term memory loss. He must have forgotten after 15 minutes. I am not shocked. We had a detailed meet,” Wangchuk shared.

Meanwhile, Wangchuk also took a dig at Aamir’s reputation for immersing himself deeply into his characters. “We have heard that he enters deeply into his characters. Maybe he was so deeply into his Ghajini character that he forgot that he attended the award function where I was awarded. We had a detailed meet and we discussed a lot of ideas,” he added.

Notably, Wangchuk also explained why he believes their interaction could have influenced certain elements of Aamir’s character in 3 Idiots and it not necessarily would have been his direct biography or based completely on him. “This is what is called influence and inspiration. Maybe he would have taken some parts (of his life) and added in the script. Maybe he didn’t tell his team that he saw all this and spoke with me. He would have shared he has added these things just like that. So, the writers and the director wouldn’t have known that Aamir added these details after meeting someone and discussing with him. That’s why he must have forgotten. It doesn’t matter to me,” he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Wangchuk’s latest remarks have once again brought the debate into focus, with the innovator maintaining that he had met Aamir before the movie and that the two had discussed several ideas during their meeting.

In further updates, For the unversed, Aamir’s comments came in July shortly after Omi Vaidya, who played Chatur in 3 Idiots , shared that the superstar’s character was inspired from Sonam Wangchuk. It was a period when Sonam was on a hunger strike during the students’ protest in response to the leak of NEET question paper.

title: Toxic box office collection Day 5: Yash film crosses ₹200 cr mark, beats Vijay's Jana Nayagan, Suriya's Karuppu
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Toxic ticket-window earnings Day 5: Geetu Mohandas and Yash’s Toxic : A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups rolled out in theatres on Wednesday amid high expectations. On its opening day, the movie minted over ₹ 101 crore rupees at the ticket-window in India, surpassing the opening of Dhurandhar: The Revenge. Given its massive start, there were expectations that the movie would go on to break several box-office records. However, Toxic witnessed a major drop in collections on its second day and has continued to see a decline in its daily earnings since then.

Adding to this, Toxic ticket-window earnings Day 5: Yash plays lead role in Geetu Mohandas' directorial. Toxic ticket-window earnings Day 5 According to Sacnilk, Toxic had collected a net ₹ 19.93 crore rupees in India by 9 pm on Sunday. This takes the movie's total India net collection to ₹ 211.03 Cr so far, while its India gross collection stands at ₹ 251.77 Cr .

Meanwhile, The movie recorded an overall theatre occupancy of 25.7% on Sunday and was screened across 15,436 shows. Although the movie has crossed the ₹ 200 crore rupees mark in India net collections, its daily collections have continued to decline since its record opening.

Notably, Looking at the language-wise breakdown, Toxic had the maximum number of shows in Hindi, with 11,210 screenings. The Hindi version collected ₹ 12.37 crore rupees and recorded 24% occupancy. The Kannada version, meanwhile, had 1,294 shows. It collected ₹ 6.12 crore rupees on Sunday, making it the second-highest contributor to the movie's Day 5 India net collection.
As per the latest buzz, In Tamil, Toxic was screened across 1,404 shows and collected ₹ 49 lakh. The Telugu version had 1,528 shows and minted ₹ 95 lakh.

In further updates, Toxic opened its theatrical run with a massive ₹ 101.10 crore rupees net collection in India on Day 1. However, the movie's collections dropped sharply on Thursday, when it collected ₹ 37.65 crore rupees, registering a 62.8% fall from its opening-day figure.

On top of that, The downward trend continued on Friday, with the movie collecting ₹ 27.20 crore rupees. On Saturday, Toxic fell further and collected ₹ 25.15 crore rupees net in India. With ₹ 18.37 crore rupees already collected by 8:30 pm on Sunday, the movie's daily earnings have continued to decline despite the weekend.

Toxic has collected less than half of what Yash's last juggernaut, KGF Chapter 2, collected within five days of its rollout in India. KGF Chapter 2 had minted ₹ 430.15 crore rupees in net collections in India within five days of its rollout.

title: Manisha Koirala urges international community to support Nepal after devastating floods: ‘We need tourism’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Manisha Koirala has asked the international community to come together and help Nepal after the devastating flash floods of August 26 that affected the mountainous Nepal -Tibet border region.

Adding to this, Manisha Koirala spoke during In Solidarity with Nepal event, in Kathmandu. (Pic: PTI) (@sadhguru) 'Global warming is real' Manisha spoke at Sadhguru's In Solidarity with Nepal event in Kathmandu on Sunday. She urged the three nations — India, China and Nepal — to come together and work towards tackling global warming to help avert such disasters in the future.

Meanwhile, As per PTI report, Manisha shared, "The global warming is real. This is not just some distant issue. I request that we, as human beings and great neighbors, China, India, and Nepal somehow join hands in this and do something collectively. We are so interconnected, and so we must work together to try to prevent disasters like this. I hope and pray that we become better people and that we help others just as we ourselves would want to be helped."

Notably, Manisha also urged the international community to come forward and help Nepal in various ways, including by visiting the country and contributing to its tourism industry, which in turn would support the livelihoods of local people.

As per the latest buzz, She shared, "Beyond this, I want to request the entire international community, that you have been so kind and loving toward Nepal time and time again. I pray that your love and support continue. As a nation, we need people to visit our country, we need tourism. We don't want to be known merely as a country that is full of disasters or constantly facing hardship. We want to be known for our beautiful weather, Himalayas, great people, nature, the culture, traditions. Yes, there is a calamity near the Nepal border, but tourism is our lifeblood. I hope and encourage the international community to travel to Nepal once again."

In further updates, The death toll from the flash floods and related disasters in Nepal and Tibet has risen to 800, with more than 3,000 people still reported missing, according to The Associated Press, citing officials. The floods struck the mountainous region near the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday, causing widespread devastation and leaving communities in the affected areas struggling to cope with the aftermath.

On top of that, The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Saturday shared that 149 Indian nationals had been rescued in Nepal. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal shared the update on social media and posted a list containing the names of the 149 rescued Indian nationals.

Manisha Koirala is a Nepalese star, who has majorly worked in Hindi cinema. She made her acting debut with the Nepali movie Pheri Bhetaula in 1989 and made her Hindi movie debut with Saudagar in 1991. She went on to establish herself as one of the leading actors of the 1990s with films such as 1942: A Love Story, Bombay, Khamoshi: The Musical, Dil Se.., Mann and Gupt: The Hidden Truth. She was last seen in Sanjay Leela Bhansali's web show Heeramandi.

Meanwhile, She captioned the post, "I am getting back to work soon and I am definitely going to miss all of this!😭😭❤️."
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rashmika Mandanna (@rashmika_mandanna)

As per the latest buzz, While reports of Rashmika getting injured on set surfaced in July, on August 3, the star posted on Instagram to share an update about her health. She wrote a long note explaining her injury. She wrote, "Hie guyssss!🥰❤️ Injuries suck.. 😩 and I was really hoping that no one will get to know.. but well 🐒🤷🏻‍♀️ Sorry I’ve been MIA 🐒 but hieeee! I’m hereeee!🙋🏻‍♀️😁 It happened awhile ago ya and this is my 3rd injury back to back.. 🤦🏻‍♀️ I should definitely learn to treat my body like a human body and not some machine.. 🤦🏻‍♀️💆🏻‍♀️ But well umm the injury is basically.. ummm how do I explain it.. (make way for the biology teacher🙋🏻‍♀️🐒🤣) so there are 4 tendons on each side of your hip that connects your hip to your leg and one of those tendons on my right hip apparently had detached and that has to attach again, for me to be able to lift my leg up and stuff.. and this happened during my dance shoot for Mysaa."

In further updates, Calling Mysaa 'the most aggressive movie' she has ever done, she wrote, "Don’t worry.. it hurts but it’s not unbearable or something.. so ya that’s that.. and I feel like this is god saying you’ll never take a break if it’s left to you so here.. let me do it for you! You know all these injuries I’ve had is random af - freak accidents what are the odds."

On top of that, Calling the time out to tend to her health a 'forced holiday', she wrote, "Not complaining at all! 🐒💃🏻 I’ve been doing a lot of puzzles - had no idea I were this good with them.. 😎 Really really trying not to put on weight cz well I workout and run like a beast which keeps me in a decent shape and now I won’t be able to workout or run for awhile 😞😭 and if I can’t workout then what do I doooo.. I eat.. and I become a dessert monster.. so uh hoooo! Well that’s about it.. what else did I miss.. nothing na.. if anything I’ll update soon. Love ya! Don’t worry ok.. Biggest loves and kisses and hugs."

Before her injury, Rashmika had been juggling a handful of films. She has Ranabaali and Mysaa in the pipeline.Mysaa is an emotional action thriller set against the backdrop of the Gond tribes. Rashmika plays the lead role in the movie as a Gond woman, a bold character that will be a departure from her previous performances.

title: Why Toxic is more than just another gangster drama: 5 reasons to watch Yash’s latest
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
From its powerhouse performances to its ambitious visual scale, here are five reasons why Toxic deserves to be experienced on the big screen.

Adding to this, 1. A gutsy movie that dares to tell its story differently Toxic doesn’t take the familiar route. It is bold in its storytelling and builds its narrative in a way that gradually reveals the many layers of its world and characters. The movie moves beyond the conventional gangster drama, bringing together action, emotion, love, and family against a larger-than-life backdrop.

Meanwhile, 2. It’s a movie you may want to watch twice There is plenty happening beneath the surface in Toxic . The storytelling is layered and deliberately complex, with details, character motivations and narrative threads that may reveal themselves differently on a second viewing. It is the kind of movie that invites you to revisit its world and piece together the larger picture.

Notably, 3. A performance-heavy movie led by Yash and an impressive ensemble At its centre is Yash, and Toxic is very much a showcase of the star. But the movie also gives its ensemble plenty to work with. Nayanthara brings a fearless intensity to her part, Kiara Advani leaves a striking impression, and Huma Qureshi delivers a performance that is haunting and powerful. title: Rajat Dalal bangs Thar into car blocking his way in Faridabad parking: ‘Roz ka drama hai’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

YouTuber and Bigg Boss 18 contestant Rajat Dalal often finds himself embroiled in controversies. This time, he posted videos of himself banging his Thar into another vehicle after it blocked his way in a parking area in Sector 16, Faridabad, Haryana.

Adding to this, Rajat Dalal had participated in Bigg Boss 18. Why did Rajat Dalal bang his Thar into another car? Rajat shared multiple videos on his Instagram Stories. The first video showed his parked Thar blocked by two cars at the front and back, leaving him with no room to drive out of the parking space. In the caption, Rajat mentioned that he faces this issue daily. He wrote, "Rooz ka drama hai. Everyday they find my car only to block."

Meanwhile, The next video showed him banging his Thar into the car blocking it in the front before driving away. In the caption, he mentioned that he waited for the owner for 45-50 minutes to come and remove the car. However, when the owner did not arrive and had also not left a contact number on the car, he decided to bang into it and drive off. The caption read, “Patiently waited for 45-50 minutes, no contact number, nothing.”

Notably, The few videos that followed showed Rajat Dalal struggling with people who had allegedly parked their vehicles incorrectly in the lane on multiple occasions in the past. He explained the situation further with a note, "It is not a promotional video or a scripted thing. This is the case with the parking everyday. This is not an aerial shot taken by a drone. This was recorded from the 3rd floor of the gym. Ek limit hote hai har cheez ki (There is a limit to everything)."

As per the latest buzz, This isn't the first time Rajat has come under scrutiny for his behaviour on the road. In 2024, Rajat was accused of striking a bike rider with his car and continuing to drive without stopping while allegedly driving at a high speed. Before this, Rajat was arrested and later rolled out on bail for allegedly kidnapping and assaulting an 18-year-old student over an Instagram post.

In further updates, Rajat Dalal is an Indian powerlifter and fitness influencer. He has won multiple national and international championships. title: Rajkumar Santoshi rejects Shabana Azmi's theory on Sunny Deol's Muslim role in Batwara 1947: 'Even Big B played it'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Sunny Deol's latest outing, Batwara 1947 , was among the most anticipated films of the year, but it received mixed reviews from critics and its ticket-window performance also remained subpar. Of late, Shabana Azmi blamed the movie's ticket-window failure on the audience not accepting Sunny Deol playing a Muslim character in the movie, as it goes against his “action patriot” image. Now, the movie's director, Rajkumar Santoshi, has reacted to the same.

Adding to this, Sunny Deol, Shabana Azmi and Preity Zinta played lead roles in Batwara 1947. 'Makes no sense to me' In conversation with Variety India, Rajkumar rejected Shabana's theory and cited how even a superstar like Amitabh Bachchan has played Muslim characters in the past. He shared, “It makes no sense to me. Amitabh Bachchan played a Muslim hero in ‘Coolie.’ So many of Manmohan Desai’s films had Muslim heroes. Are we at a point where we cannot accept a hero from the other community? We are sensible, good people, educated people. How are they saying there’s a big mistake in the movie?”

Meanwhile, In the same interview, however, Rajkumar accepted that 'we have become far less tolerant and inclusive'. Talking about his 2001 movie Lajja and how today's audience may not accept the movie's segment based on the Ramayana, he shared, “We have become far less tolerant and inclusive as a people. You should look at the filmmaker’s intent and what the writer wants to say. I’m a Hindu. I go to the temple. My son’s name is Ram. I am not against any faith. But I want to take the best of every faith. Whatever the saints have tried to say about faith, it is always about equality. Hinduism has always been about inclusiveness, not exclusion.”

Notably, In conversation with Zoom, Shabana Azmi spoke about Batwara 1947's failure and shared, “The thing is that you cannot accept Sunny Deol as a Muslim. In Coolie and in many other films, Amitabh Bachchan very comfortably played Muslim characters. In Deewaar, he put 786 and that was accepted. So how do we understand this? Are they creating an environment where such decisions are being taken on purpose? I am not able to understand. I am surprised at how people are reacting to it. Even the ones who have watched the movie think Sunny Deol is playing a Pakistani. He is not. It is simply not registering in their heads."

As per the latest buzz, The movie sees Sunny Deol play the character of Sikandar Mirza, who finds a Hindu woman, Mai, played by Shabana Azmi, living at the house allotted to him after Partition. He takes it upon himself to save Mai from religious extremists in Pakistan.

title: Arshad Warsi says Kangana Ranaut came up with the idea of nepotism and it became big: ‘It’s not easy for star kids'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood star Arshad Warsi has never been one to shy away from calling things as he sees them. Speaking about the much-debated conversation around nepotism, the star acknowledged that star kids may get an easier entry into the industry but insisted that staying successful ultimately comes down to talent. He also opened up about seeing the pressure of being a star kid through the eyes of his own children.

Adding to this, Arshad Warsi says Kangana Ranaut made the idea of nepotism big. Arshad Warsi talks about nepotism In a podcast with Filmygyan, when asked about the nepotism debate when he entered the industry, Arshad shared nepotism was not a topic when he started his career. He added, "Kangana came out with the idea of nepotism, and then it got big, and everyone started talking about it. Yes, it's there, but it doesn't bother me. My heart tells me at the end of the day it's about how talented you are and that's how far you will go."

Meanwhile, He added, "I also know that it's not easy for a star kid. The expectations are so high. It's like today I see that happening with my child. The impression other people have of them, because they are my kids, is that they have to be good actors. I feel like, 'oh my god, don't say that,' because everyone has their own personalities. Too much is expected of star kids, and they have to live up to too many people's expectations. It's not fair. The maximum that can happen to them is a door gets opened faster, but if you are not talented, it shuts down quickly."

Notably, Arshad further opened up that he does not fear success or failure for his children, but instead wants them to become good actors and be talented enough to know their craft well. The star added that he wants his children to be prepared, as young actors entering the industry are increasingly well-prepared.
As per the latest buzz, Arshad has two children, a son named Zeke Warsi and a daughter named Zene Zoe Warsi.

In further updates, The star is gearing up for the rollout of his soon-to-release movie Ghamasaan. Helmed by Tigmanshu Dhulia, the movie also stars Pratik Gandhi, Rajpal Yadav and Ishita Dutta in lead roles. The movie is scheduled to rollout on ZEE5 on September 11.

On top of that, Arshad will also be seen in King. Helmed by Siddharth Anand, the movie stars Shah Rukh Khan in the lead role, alongside Deepika Padukone, Suhana Khan, Abhishek Bachchan and others in key roles. The movie marks SRK's return to the big screen after two years and is set to rollout in theatres on December 24. It will clash at the ticket-window with Nagarjuna's King100, which marks the superstar's 100th movie.

title: 'Short-term memory loss hua hoga': Sonam Wangchuk mocks Aamir Khan's ‘we never met before 3 Idiots' claim
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In July, Bollywood star Aamir Khan denied knowing climate activist Sonam Wangchuk during the making of 3 Idiots and also denied that the movie was based on him. Hours after his statement, a video of Aamir and Sonam meeting in 2008 surfaced online. Now, in a podcast with Prakhar Gupta, Sonam took a sly dig at Aamir while responding to his claims.

Adding to this, Sonam Wangchuk says he's not surprised by Aamir Khan's 'we never met' before 3 Idiots claim. Sonam Wangchuk roasts Aamir Khan Sonam reacted to Aamir's ‘we never met’ claims and shared, "When he shared that we hadn’t even met, some videos later emerged in which he was watching one of my speeches while dressed in the Ghajini outfit. Shayad woh Ghajini outfit mein the toh short-term memory loss huwa hoga, 15 min aad bhul gaye honge. Toh, mai hairaan nahi hoon. Warna bahot detail mein mile the hum (Perhaps he was in the Ghajini outfit, so he had some short-term memory loss and forgot for 15 minutes or so. So, I’m not surprised. Otherwise, we had met and discussed things in great detail)."

Meanwhile, Recalling Aamir’s statement, Sonam shared, “We’ve heard that he gets so deeply into his characters. So perhaps he got so immersed in Ghajini that when he came to the award function where I was receiving an award, he may have forgotten about me too. Otherwise, we met at length and discussed a lot of ideas. And I wouldn’t say that he based it on or made a biography of... this is what you call inspiration. He had a script, so he must have added into it. Perhaps his co-writers or directors didn’t realise that he had added an idea he had picked up somewhere, after meeting someone or having a conversation. It doesn’t make any difference to me. Let it go.”

Notably, During an interaction at the British Movie Institute (BFI), Aamir Khan was asked about activist Sonam Wangchuk and his ongoing hunger strike. Responding to the question, Aamir denied knowing the activist during the making of 3 Idiots.

As per the latest buzz, He shared, “No, that’s not true, actually. That is a misconception. I didn’t know about Mr Sonam Wangchuk at that time when we were doing the movie. I know that; I saw a video of Chatur. Just of late, he shared that… No, he’s wrong. Maybe that’s what Chatur was thinking, but I want to tell you neither did Raju, nor Abhijat (one of the two writers), nor I, we didn’t know about Sonam. However, what Mr Sonam is doing is good work anyway. He doesn’t need to be based on the character of 3 Idiots for us to respect him and the work he’s done.”

In further updates, Directed by Rajkumar Hirani, 3 Idiots is one of Bollywood’s most loved coming-of-age films. Rolled out in 2009, the movie stars Aamir Khan, R Madhavan, Sharman Joshi, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Boman Irani in pivotal roles.

On top of that, Set against the backdrop of an engineering college, the movie follows three friends, Rancho (Aamir), Farhan (Madhavan) and Raju (Sharman), as they navigate academic pressure, friendship, family expectations and the race for success. Rancho’s unconventional approach to education challenges the system’s obsession with marks and ranks, while Farhan and Raju struggle with their own fears and ambitions.
The movie was both a critical and commercial success and went on to become one of the highest-grossing Indian films of its time.

title: Actor Anud Singh Dhaka’s love affair with Lucknow University: Playing LU student thrice is really something special
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Star Anud Singh Dhaka , who was born and brought up in Bhopal and studied at St. Xavier’s College in Mumbai, says Lucknow University has been instrumental in shaping his career.

Adding to this, The star says, “Kuch to hai, woh shayad aagey jaakar samajh mein aayega! Now, I know so much about the university that during the shoot, someone asked, ‘Where is the chemistry department?’ and I was like, ‘Aagey se right lelo!’ They asked, ‘How do you know that?’ and I was like, ‘Apna purana rishta hai university se.’
Meanwhile, From his first project that got him noticed to his most recent show, he has played a Lucknow University student.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Anud Singh Dhaka (@anudsinghdhaka)

As per the latest buzz, “For the first time, I shot for Taj Mahal 1989 , where I played a psychology student. That show established me in the industry and was directed by Pushpendra Nath Misra, a Lucknowite. Then, producer-director Saurabh Tiwari sir, who is also from the city, cast me as the lead in Love J Action (2021) and also in my last show, Psycho Saiyaan (2026),” he says, and adds, “Of late, I wrapped up shooting for Sachin Pandey’s show Tamanche Pe Disco , where I again play a small-town lad who becomes an LU student.”

In further updates, Besides shooting three projects at LU, he has shot two more projects in the city. “After the shoot of Taj Mahal 1989 , I got a chance to shoot an ad with Mr Amitabh Bachchan for KBC . Incidentally, he was shooting for Gulabo Sitabo (2020) in Lucknow, so I came down to shoot here. It was my journey from a college in Lucknow to the hot seat.”

On top of that, Before Tamanche Pe Disco , he shot for a show, Dil Cheer Ke Dekh , which he filmed in various parts of Lucknow and Barabanki. “It is also by Sachin sir, where, interestingly, I also play a student, but this time I did not shoot at LU. We shot the interiors in a different college, but the exterior shots are of LU—probably under a different name.”

“Sometimes, I joke with my co-actors that if I get more projects here, I will buy a house here. After shooting five projects, I know so much about the city, its culture, people, and the local cuisine. From April till August, I have shot two series back-to-back and literally established a mini-home here. I am a St. Xavier’s alumnus and have shot there once, but here, I have already done three projects and counting. I am seriously thinking about pursuing a philosophy course at LU.”

title: Chandrachur Singh files FIR against relatives, alleges grandfather's will was forged to deny father inheritance
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Adding to this, Chandrachur Singh had filed FIR against relatives. Signature of grandfather forged In his complaint filed at Rorawar police station on Friday, Singh alleged that the signature of his grandfather, Thakur Harender Pal Singh, a prominent landowner of Jalalpur village on the outskirts of Aligarh, was forged in 1997 when he was critically ill and allegedly not in a position to sign documents.

In further updates, Talking to reporters on Friday evening, Singh shared he had collected sufficient evidence to substantiate his allegations. He also shared that after lodging the FIR, he recorded his statement with the police.

On top of that, The dispute had come to light last year, when Gaytri Devi had rejected the allegations as false and accused Chandrachur of trying to falsely implicate her. She had also maintained that the will was genuine.
